note: FRAMES is a process-lifetime static HashMap<i64,Frame>. open() inserts every frame (lib.rs:44); the only remover is close() (lib.rs:73), which is called by the JVM. kotlin/shop/Encoder.kt:11-14 returns early for frames over MAX_INLINE_BYTES (16384, more than 255 lines) without calling Native.close, so bulk frames stay in FRAMES forever. Missing pairing: close for every open on the bulk-lane path. Not exercised by DLA: the cdylib needs a JVM, and the rust harness has no lib or bin target to drive. Class of repair: release the handle on the bulk path too. The jvm worker owns the Kotlin side.
Frame.bytes is owned by the FRAMES entry (see rust/F2) and is freed when the entry is removed. It has no independent lifetime: any retention comes from F2.

remedy: Run a JVM-driven replay (./build.sh run N, with N large enough to produce frames over 16384 bytes) and trend Native.live()/liveBytes() (nativeLive column in Stats.checkpoint) with a non-leak sibling N-WARM; the rust harness cannot load a cdylib without a JVM. Expected: nativeLive grows with the count of bulk frames and drops to 0 only if close is called on the bulk path.
